bull.b: The sharp revenue rebound and higher gross margin indicate stronger operating performance and improved economics versus the prior period. If maintained, this combination can support progress toward sustainable profitability and provide a stronger base for funding future operations.

Positive operating cash flow marks a constructive change from the heavy cash burn reported during 2023–2025. Although free cash flow remains thin, internally generated cash can reduce reliance on external financing if the improved operating trend persists.

bull.t: Improved Q2 operating results and equity
bull.b: The latest reported quarter showed broader improvement than revenue alone, including stronger gross profit, modest operating profit, and higher equity. That suggests the recovery is reaching several financial statement lines, which may improve resilience over the next few quarters.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated durable earnings power: net income remains negative and EBITDA is only modestly positive. The multi-year swing from profit to losses makes the current recovery less dependable and leaves results vulnerable if operating conditions weaken.

Debt remains slightly above equity, so leverage continues to constrain financial flexibility despite improving from the much higher 2025 level. This capital structure can limit the company’s ability to absorb weaker results or pursue expansion without additional financing.

bear.t: Free cash flow cushion is very limited
bear.b: The move to barely positive free cash flow is encouraging but provides little protection against softer margins or a reversal in working capital. Sharp deterioration from the prior annual period also shows that cash generation is not yet consistent enough to support a durable cushion.
